comment: Fleet-infra finding patterns for ops/fleet-infra-findings.py (SCHED-GAP-128). `pattern` must match the row TITLE; the optional `requires` co-signal may come from the row body. `exclude` matches titles that NAME this class in order to FIX it (the tracking rows) — those are never collapsed and never counted as duplicates.

patterns.name: port_pool
patterns.why: Port-pool exhaustion is a property of the SHARED host's per-user port allocations. The `requires` half is what keeps a project's own port-allocation bug (a service binding :8080 twice) out of the fleet bucket.

patterns.name: dropped_config
patterns.why: A config that stopped reaching the running component is a delivery-layer fault of the shared host. Local repo config bugs carry no host/substrate token.

patterns.name: stale_binary
patterns.why: The fleet's stale-binary class is the QA/host binary being older than the commit it must serve. A PROJECT's own 'deployed binary stale vs HEAD' (e.g. ~/.local/bin/dagger) is project-local and must NOT be swept — the `requires` half is that discriminator, and it deliberately does NOT accept a bare 'bunker' mention: this fleet's prose says 'bunker' in almost every row, so a bare token would sweep project rows that merely discuss the host.

patterns.name: gateway_auth
patterns.why: The Hermes gateway and its key are fleet-wide infrastructure: every lane authenticates through the same gateway, so an auth rejection is never one project's finding.
